raw_response:
I’ve been farming this land for 40 years, since I was 21. My old man taught me, and I mostly do what he did, adjusting a bit based on what I see with my own eyes. I only finished primary school, so I don’t know those fancy formulas the extension people talk about. I know this 7.8 mu. It’s just me and my wife now — our son works in Shijiazhuang — so labor is tight. We can’t afford to mess around.

This year, like always, I’ll plant wheat right after National Day, around October 5th to 10th. I buy the improved Jinmai seed from the shop in town — about 25 jin per mu, costs roughly 30 yuan per mu. Before planting, I plow once after the maize comes off and harrow it level. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that’s about 50 kg per mu, the 15-15-15 kind. Then in spring, when the wheat turns green around March, if it looks a bit yellow I’ll topdress with half a bag of urea, about 20 kg per mu. My neighbor Old Wang says he uses less fertilizer now to save money, but I’d rather put a bit more than risk a bad year. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps.

For water, I pump from my well, but electricity costs add up. I irrigate three times for wheat: once right after planting to help it settle, once at jointing in April, and once at grain filling in May if it’s dry. That usually does it. I spray herbicide once in early spring — the weeds would choke us otherwise.

Then in early June, the wheat comes off and there’s no time to waste. Sometimes I only have four or five days. I hire the planter from the village machinery group for maize — 20 yuan per mu — because at my age I can’t plant 7.8 mu by hand that fast. I use hybrid maize seed, about 45 yuan per mu. One bag of compound fertilizer per mu goes down at planting, then if it doesn’t rain and the plants look hungry at the big trumpet stage, I’ll add some urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. Maize gets two irrigations, maybe three if July is scorching. I watch for armyworm — if I see them, I spray insecticide. Otherwise I keep it simple.

We do almost all the work ourselves, but I might hire 2–3 days for harvest and another 2 days for maize planting if the weather window is tight. Hired labor is 120 yuan per day now. I have to watch my cash — we need money for food and medicine too. Total input costs will be around 5,500 yuan this year. I expect about 420 kg per mu of wheat and 480 kg per mu of maize if the weather cooperates. Not fancy, but it keeps us going.
